title: Ground Emergencies
summary: Start malfunctions, ground emergencies, emergency shutdowns, and egress procedures.
overview: This event builds on basic cockpit procedures by introducing abnormal starts and ground emergencies. You will practice identifying no starts, hung starts, hot starts, fire indications, emergency shutdown procedures, and emergency ground egress while continuing to build checklist discipline and CRM.

studyNotes.headline: Discussion items
studyNotes.summary: Focus on recognizing a bad start early, taking immediate abort actions, and knowing when ground emergencies require an engine shutdown or egress.

items.text: The PMU will often automatically terminate a bad start, but you still need to recognize the indications and be ready to manually abort.
Three primary start malfunctions:

children.text: No Start: No ITT rise within 10 seconds after fuel flow indications.
Hung Start: N1 stops increasing normally.
Hot Start: ITT is rising rapidly and appears likely to exceed 1000°C.

items.text: You should also manually abort if:

children.text: ITT appears likely to stay between 871°C and 1000°C for more than 5 seconds.
The red BATT BUS warning appears during start.
The ST READY advisory extinguishes during the start sequence.
The PCL is moved incorrectly during start.

items.text: Any overtemperature should be noted and reported to maintenance.
If a start must be aborted:

children.text: Or reselect STARTER switch to AUTO/RESET if appropriate.

items.text: After any aborted start where fuel was introduced, perform a motoring run.
Motoring Run Procedure:
The goal of the motoring run is to clear residual fuel and lower ITT.

sections.title: Loss of START READY During Start

items.text: Ensure the ST READY advisory remains on for at least 3 seconds before selecting AUTO/RESET.
If the ST READY advisory extinguishes at any point during the start sequence, the PMU no longer provides automatic start protection.
Once ST READY is lost, the start must be manually aborted.
If the PCL is still before idle, abort by moving the PCL to OFF or selecting AUTO/RESET.
If the PCL is already past the idle gate, abort with PCL OFF.
The red BATT BUS warning during start is a serious indication.
It may appear before the displays fail.
If it appears, MFD failure and the inability to monitor the start may be imminent.
Immediately abort the start.
The primary indication of an engine fire is illumination of the FIRE annunciators.
Other signs include:

children.text: Notification from tower, ground crew, or another aircraft.

items.text: If a fire is suspected, execute Emergency Engine Shutdown on the Ground and Emergency Ground Egress if required.

sections.title: Emergency Engine Shutdown on the Ground

items.text: Use this procedure for:
Immediate actions:
The aircraft has 0/0 ejection capability, but ground egress should be completed once the aircraft is stopped and the engine is shut down.
Standard procedure:
If the canopy cannot be opened:

children.text: BAT, GEN, and AUX BAT switches OFF.

items.text: Oxygen mask on and visor down before activating the CFS.
Both cockpits must activate their own CFS handles if both transparencies need to fracture.
The Canopy Fracturing System clears a path through the canopy during ejection.
Front cockpit uses a stronger explosive charge because the front windscreen is thicker.
Rear cockpit uses a lighter charge because the rear transparency is thinner.
Minimum uncontrolled ejection altitude is 6000 feet AGL.
Minimum controlled ejection altitude is 2000 feet AGL.
Controlled ejections rely heavily on CRM to split checklist tasks and maximize survivability.
The ejection seat is a Martin-Baker system capable of 0/0 ejection.
Full strap-in with all flight equipment.
